answer.rationale: Write-path p99 at 5x began ~30 minutes after the new release and has lasted 90 minutes, so a write-path regression is the leading hypothesis. memory_b1 is the only inherited case that restored a checkout/write failure mode by returning to a known-stable build without customer impact, which matches the objective of sustained availability without dropping customer writes. Verify that record before committing in case the archive has caveats about peak settlement. Competing explanations remain open: daily settlement peak and heavy writes could be capacity (memory_b3), but that lesson was headroom provisioned before the peak, not a mid-surge add, and we get only one intervention. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing fast would shed writes (memory_b4). Staged gating (memory_b6) argues for care, but a tiny canary would leave most settlement traffic on the suspected build for another full window; a complete rollback is the one action that can actually restore availability now. Flag downstream settlement-value risk because we are changing the write path at daily peak, and keep uncertainty explicit until rollback either clears latency or does not.
